content.title: Everything you need to know about Opening Day 2026
content.text: It's almost time for two of the best words in baseball: Opening Day!The curtain will rise on the 2026 regular season on March 25 with a special Opening Night showdown between the Yankees and Giants. MLB's 28 other teams will play their first game of the season at some point over the following two days.Here is everything you need to know for the beginning of the season. The 2026 season is here! Lock in your tickets to the best games! When does the 2026 regular season begin? The Giants will host the Yankees on Wednesday, March 25 as part of MLB Opening Night. This standalone game between two historic franchises will air on Netflix, marking the streaming service's first regular-season big league game. Netflix will also broadcast MLB's Opening Night game for the 2027 and '28 seasons.First pitch for the 2026 Opening Night game at Oracle Park is scheduled for 8:05 p.m. ET.When will it be Opening Day for every team? Once we get past Opening Night, Opening Day baseball will continue over the next two days for the other 28 Major League clubs.Twenty-two teams will begin their season on Thursday, March 26. That 11-game slate is highlighted by Tarik Skubal and the Tigers visiting the Padres, and the Dodgers starting their quest for a three-peat at home versus the D-backs. That D-backs-Dodgers game will air on NBC at 8:30 p.m. ET.Six more teams -- the Athletics, Blue Jays, Braves, Marlins, Rockies and Royals -- will play their Opening Day game on Friday, March 27.Saturday, March 28 is the first day on the schedule when all 30 teams will be in action. Tracking every Opening Day starter for 2026 What is my team's season-opening matchup? Here is a look at the first game of the 2026 season for all 30 MLB teams: Angels: March 26 at Astros (4:10 p.m. ET) Astros: March 26 vs. Angels (4:10 p.m. ET) Athletics: March 27 at Blue Jays (7:07 p.m. ET) Blue Jays: March 27 vs. Athletics (7:07 p.m. ET) Braves: March 27 vs. Royals (7:15 p.m. ET) Brewers: March 26 vs. White Sox (2:10 p.m. ET) Cardinals: March 26 vs. Rays (4:15 p.m. ET) Cubs: March 26 vs. Nationals (2:20 p.m. ET) Diamondbacks: March 26 at Dodgers (8:30 p.m. ET) Dodgers: March 26 vs. Diamondbacks (8:30 p.m. ET) Giants: March 25 vs. Yankees (8:05 p.m. ET) Guardians: March 26 at Mariners (10:10 p.m. ET) Mariners: March 26 vs. Guardians (10:10 p.m. ET) Marlins: March 27 vs. Rockies (7:10 p.m. ET) Mets: March 26 vs. Pirates (1:15 p.m. ET) Nationals: March 26 at Cubs (2:20 p.m. ET) Orioles: March 26 vs. Twins (3:05 p.m. ET) Padres: March 26 vs. Tigers (4:10 p.m. ET) Phillies: March 26 vs. Rangers (4:15 p.m. ET) Pirates: March 26 at Mets (1:15 p.m. ET) Rangers: March 26 at Phillies (4:15 p.m. ET) Rays: March 26 at Cardinals (4:15 p.m. ET) Reds: March 26 vs. Red Sox (4:10 p.m. ET) Red Sox: March 26 at Reds (4:10 p.m. ET) Rockies: March 27 at Marlins (7:10 p.m. ET) Royals: March 27 at Braves (7:15 p.m. ET) Tigers: March 26 at Padres (7:10 p.m. ET) Twins: March 26 at Orioles (3:05 p.m. ET) White Sox: March 26 at Brewers (2:10 p.m. ET) Yankees: March 25 at Giants (8:05 p.m. ET) Skenes back to Cy Young form in win after tough Opening Day start7:33 PM UTCCINCINNATI -- Pirates ace Paul Skenes rebounded from the shortest outing of his career to post five strong innings Wednesday and earn his first win of the season, 8-3, against Cincinnati at Great American Ball Park.After allowing five runs on four hits, walking two and hitting a batter while retiring just two batters last Thursday, Skenes (1-1) allowed just one run on three hits, striking out five and walking two. He tossed 77 pitches (51 strikes) and lowered his season ERA from 67.50 to 9.53. Skenes left with a 4-1 lead thanks to an Oneil Cruz three-run homer off Cincinnati starter Andrew Abbott (0-1) in the first. Pirates Home Opener is Friday vs. the Orioles -- Get your tickets now! Mason Montgomery relieved Skenes to start the sixth, and allowed a pinch-hit two-run homer to Eugenio Suárez as the Reds cut the Pirates’ lead to one run. But Isaac Mattson, Justin Lawrence and Gregory Soto finished off the final 3 1/3 innings for Pittsburgh’s first series victory of the season.The Pirates have Thursday off before their home opener Friday afternoon against Baltimore.Bryan Reynolds blasted a two-run homer deep to the seats in right in a four-run ninth for his 140th as a Pirate, moving him into sole possession of ninth place all-time in Pirates history.Skenes didn’t give up a hit until Elly De La Cruz swatted a 90.1 mph changeup to right field for a single to open the bottom of the fourth. After Sal Stewart’s grounder moved De La Cruz to second, Nathaniel Lowe doubled him home, snapping Skenes’ scoreless streak against Cincinnati at 31 innings, dating to his first career start against the Reds on June 17, 2024.Coming into Wednesday’s game, the opponent figured to be the perfect elixir for the flame-throwing Pittsburgh ace after his shortest career outing six days earlier against the Mets in Queens.In five previous starts against the Reds, Skenes was 4-0 with a 0.31 ERA, covering 29 innings. He struck out 40 and walked just two batters. Skenes had not allowed a run against Cincinnati since the first inning of his first start against the Reds.Like his Opening Day start last Thursday, Skenes had an early lead to work with, this time thanks to Cruz belting his third homer of the series and season, and his second in as many at-bats.With two outs, Reynolds singled and Marcell Ozuna walked. Cruz then hopped all over a hanging curve from Abbott and unloaded it a Statcast-projected 407 feet to right for a 3-0 Pirates lead in the first.Skenes needed a batter to find his rhythm, walking leadoff man TJ Friedl on five pitches. But unlike his outing against the Mets, he quickly found a groove, striking out Matt McLain and De La Cruz before retiring the red-hot Stewart on a force out at second.
